clue.text: Run slowly over bit of leg, teasing

indicators.note: the jogging word is laid over the leg part, wrapping round it

parts.note: to jog is to run at a slow steady pace
the shin is the front part of the lower leg

explanation.surface: A runner eases off over an injured bit of leg while friends rib them.
explanation.definitionFit: Joshing is light-hearted mocking banter, a synonym for teasing.

clue.text: Woman article taken aboard plane

indicators.note: something taken aboard a plane ends up inside it

parts.note: a jet is a plane
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A woman's item is carried onto a flight.
explanation.definitionFit: Janet is a female given name, so an example of a woman.

clue.text: Soprano caught with hammy old novelist

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for soprano in music
C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
hammy acting is over the top, abbreviated OTT

explanation.surface: A singer is nabbed alongside an overacting writer of yesteryear.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Walter Scott, author of Ivanhoe, was a nineteenth-century Scottish writer of historical fiction.

clue.text: Hoskins to challenge authority? It's very likely!

parts.note: the setter Hoskins refers to himself, so I
to dare someone is to challenge them
having the say is having the power to decide

explanation.surface: The setter wonders aloud whether to defy the powers that be, and decides probably so.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's pseudonym stands for the first-person pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: The expression signals that the speaker thinks something probable, an idiom of supposition.

clue.text: In America, dull sauce lacks bit of va-va-voom

indicators.note: the sauce lacks a letter, so that letter is removed from it

parts.note: gravy is a meat sauce

indicators.note: a bit of the word is its opening letter here

explanation.surface: An American cook's gravy is flat because it is missing some zing.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing V from GRAVY leaves the American spelling; British English writes GREY.
explanation.definitionFit: Gray, the US spelling of grey, describes a dull, colourless shade or a dreary mood.

clue.text: Colour supplement intellectual unwrapped

parts.note: a colour supplement is a newspaper magazine, a mag

indicators.note: with its wrapping off, the word loses its outer letters

parts.note: mental means of the intellect

explanation.surface: The Sunday colour magazine reveals a brainy type with no cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colour supplement' reads as one phrase, but 'Colour' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Magenta is a purplish-red shade, an example of a colour.

clue.text: Fail to meet nurses Frank sends to wrong address

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so one word holds the other

parts.note: to miss someone is to fail to meet them
direct means frank, straightforward

explanation.surface: A mix-up means an outspoken message goes astray and nurses never get it.
explanation.definitionFit: To misdirect mail is to send it to an incorrect destination.

clue.text: Stupid-looking Observer humorist sent up a …

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means written bottom to top

parts.note: a wag is a joker
per means a, as in so much per day

explanation.surface: A newspaper columnist who mocks people, with the clue trailing into the next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Observer' looks like the newspaper but is part of the definition; the dots link to 7 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who gawps stares with open-mouthed vacancy, so is an observer looking stupid.

clue.text: … story run on gunmen breaking into local

indicators.note: the pair forces its way inside the word for a local

parts.note: a native is a local person

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
RA is the Royal Artillery, the army's gunners

explanation.surface: A tale continues: armed men burst into the village pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' tempts as a pub, a British usage; here it is a resident.
explanation.definitionFit: A narrative is an account of events, a synonym for story.

clue.text: Mess about putting Tango in a vessel for tea?

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the drinking vessel

parts.note: a cup holds tea
Tango is T in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone tips orange fizzy drink into a teacup as a prank.
explanation.walkthrough: Tango is also a British fizzy orange drink, which feeds the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To act up is to misbehave, an idiom for messing about.

clue.text: Religious revivalists releasing a song and an EP

indicators.note: the letters are let loose and freed to fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spiritual movement puts out a single and an extended-play record.
explanation.definitionFit: Neopagans revive pre-Christian nature worship, so are religious revivalists.

clue.text: Banger with puncture pulling off minor road

indicators.note: pulling off removes something from the word

parts.note: a burst is a puncture or rupture
a B-road is a minor road in Britain

explanation.surface: An old car with a flat tyre pulls off a country lane.
explanation.walkthrough: Banger is British slang for both an old car and a sausage; the definition is the sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: Wurst is German sausage, and a sausage is a banger in British slang.

clue.text: Maybe a mathematician to stagger about?

definitions.meaning: one who tots up figures, a whimsical name for a numbers person

explanation.definitionFit: One who tots numbers is jocularly an adder; to walk shakily is the everyday verb.

clue.text: Piano associated with lively wartime dance

indicators.note: a lively arrangement shakes the letters into a new order

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A pianist accompanies an energetic dance from the war years.
explanation.definitionFit: The Time Warp is the dance number from The Rocky Horror Show.

clue.text: Pale coffee brought up after meat pie?

indicators.note: the reversed coffee comes after the pie

parts.note: a pasty is a pastry case of meat, a Cornish staple

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means written bottom to top

parts.note: decaf is decaffeinated coffee

explanation.surface: Someone throws up their coffee after eating a pie.
explanation.walkthrough: A pasty is a British folded pastry with savoury filling.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasty-faced describes a sickly, washed-out complexion, so pale.

clue.text: Spoil old woman with deals on preserves

parts.note: to mar is to spoil
ma is mother, an informal old woman

indicators.note: on, as in carrying on or up to something, sets the letters in motion to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone spoils their mum by bringing home jam on special offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' is a loose signal for rearranging DEALS into LADES.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmalades are citrus jams, examples of fruit preserves.

clue.text: Dude with cropped hair

indicators.note: cropped means cut short, losing the end letter

parts.note: a mane is a long head of hair

explanation.surface: A guy with a short haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: Dude is slang for a guy, a male person.

clue.text: Support restraint on behalf of church

parts.note: a rein restrains a horse
for means on behalf of
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Backing a curb acting for the church.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinforce is to strengthen or back up, a synonym for support.

clue.text: Record-breaking institute with small margins

indicators.note: the institute letter breaks into the record, splitting it

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A research body sets a record, winning by narrow margins.
explanation.definitionFit: Lips are rims or edges, as of a cup, so margins.

clue.text: Cunning Sally shows only occasionally

indicators.note: only some letters of the name are seen, every other one

explanation.surface: A crafty woman makes rare appearances.
explanation.definitionFit: Sly means crafty and artful, a synonym for cunning.

clue.text: Firm distributing album with Island record label

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: distributing spreads the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A company handling an album from an island-based record label.
explanation.definitionFit: Columbia is a long-standing American music company issuing recordings.

clue.text: Press backs moving independent film genre

indicators.note: moving shifts one letter to a new place
backs means goes backwards, so the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to iron is to press clothes

explanation.surface: The press supports a touching independent film.
explanation.walkthrough: IRON reversed gives NORI; moving the I one place gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Noir is a style of dark, cynical crime cinema, so a kind of movie.

clue.text: Bent attorneys stealing one's paper and pens?

indicators.note: the rearranged lawyers take the number into their midst
bent means distorted, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Crooked lawyers pilfer office supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' (crooked) signals an anagram of ATTORNEYS, STATONERY, which takes I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper and pens are examples of writing materials, the question mark showing definition by example.

clue.text: In the sack, Ray made an ass-like sound

indicators.note: Ray goes in the sack, so inside the word

parts.note: the sack is slang for bed

explanation.surface: In bed, Ray let out a donkey's noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A donkey's harsh cry is its bray, so to have uttered it is to sound like an ass.

clue.text: Rubbish musical phrase hindering fine service

parts.note: a riff is a repeated musical phrase

indicators.note: the service holds back the fine letter by keeping it inside

parts.note: the RAF is the Royal Air Force, an armed service
F is short for fine, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A guitar lick is obstructing a good military operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Riffraff are disreputable people, the dregs or rubbish of society.

clue.text: Unsteady old prizefighter?

definitions.meaning: ... Marciano was a famous past boxing champion, as is the film boxer Balboa

explanation.definitionFit: Rocky means shaky; Rocky Marciano and screen boxer Rocky Balboa are old boxers.

clue.text: Beef jerky mules brought around cape

indicators.note: the rearranged animals are placed round the letter
jerky means moving in jolts, so the letters are jolted into new order

parts.note: C is short for cape on maps

explanation.surface: Dried meat is carried by mules round a headland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beef jerky' looks like one phrase, but 'jerky' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef is informal for brawn, physical strength or bulk.

clue.text: Cruise that goes all around the UK?

definitions.meaning: to cruise is to move along effortlessly

definitions.text: that goes all around the UK?

explanation.definitionFit: To coast is to glide without effort; the seashore runs round the whole island.

clue.text: Man one spotted being sat on by journalist

indicators.note: in a down clue the journalist sits above the other piece

parts.note: ED is short for editor
a die is a spotted cube

explanation.surface: A man seen being sat on by a reporter.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddie is a male given name, so an example of a man.

clue.text: Not good to be cut by head of rusty nail

indicators.note: the word is split by the letter cutting into it

parts.note: bad means not good

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A rusty-headed nail is no good, risking a cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A brad is a thin small-headed nail, an example of nail.

clue.text: Electrical retailer losing capital on satellite dish

indicators.note: losing means a letter is taken away

parts.note: Currys is a British chain of electrical shops

indicators.note: the capital letter on a word is its first

explanation.surface: An electrical shop loses money on satellite dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Satellite dish' is one item on the surface; 'dish' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Curry is a spiced meal, an example of a dish.

clue.text: Directors backing eccentric without substance

indicators.note: the directors back up the eccentric, coming after

parts.note: a card is an eccentric character
a board is a company's directors

explanation.surface: Executives support an oddball who lacks depth.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardboard characters are flat and lifeless, lacking depth.

clue.text: Yard initially dealt with missing female, then gave up

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter
missing means a letter is left out

parts.note: fielded means handled, dealt with

explanation.surface: A yard handled things without a woman, then surrendered.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield is to surrender, a synonym for giving up.

clue.text: Soldier, perhaps unwilling, to put float into river

indicators.note: the float goes into the river

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
a raft is a float

explanation.surface: A reluctant soldier is told to launch a float onto the river.
explanation.definitionFit: A draftee is a conscript, called up and not necessarily willing.
